record.text: Among the SME-Instrument-funded projects whose product is a learning game, one is aimed at qualified professionals rather than at children or everyday consumers; what does its product let them rehearse?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%serious game%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%game-based learning%') AND (p.objective ILIKE '%learn%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%educat%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%training%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: The one aimed at professionals rather than at children or consumers is abcdeSIM-VR, the SME-1 feasibility project of VirtualMedSchool (VMS) in Rotterdam, built with the Erasmus Medical Centre University Hospital and the SBOH. Its product pairs a Virtual Reality headset with a web-based simulation platform containing a serious game, so that medical and health professionals and trainees can rehearse treating virtual patients in real time under different clinical settings - emergency care skills above all - and can experiment with therapies and watch the physiological response, without any risk to real patients.
record.notes: FILTER: fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' (SME-1/SME-2, the SME Instrument phases; schema_docs lists SME-1 and SME-2 among the 56 fundingScheme values) intersected with a learning-game topic condition over the objective (serious game OR game-based learning, plus a learn/educat/training co-term - the bare gamification term is noisy). Re-executed this pass: 3 survivors, no drift from candidate hybrid-26 (3 under the SME filter, 33 corpus-wide without it). All three are SME-1, EUR 50,000 phase-1 feasibility grants. RUNTIME NOTE: the scoped path filters only structural columns, so at runtime the SME-Instrument half is the filter and the learning-game half falls to retrieval; the question is worded so that this split still works. ADJUDICATION was EXHAUSTIVE (3 <= 20, full get_project_text payload for all three). 781138 abcdeSIM-VR IN: 'a disruptive web-based platform to effectively train medical/health professionals by using serious gaming and medical simulation'; the abcdeSIM-VR adds a Virtual Reality headset so 'the medical trainee ... is fully immersed in a simulated real environment, being able to perform on virtual patients, in real-time, under different clinical settings'; report adds emergency-care skills, self-directed learning for experienced clinicians, and 'trainees are allow to experiment different therapies and see the inmediate response'. 684657 TheCityGame pilot OUT: a consumer mobile 'serious game' that rewards ordinary citizens for recycling, donating clothes, using public transport and keeping utility bills low - end users are the general public, not qualified professionals. 718990 LINGOKIDS OUT: game-based-learning language app whose learners are children aged 2 to 6; parents and educators only get tracking tools and progress reports, so the product does not let a professional rehearse anything. FILTER-DISCRIMINATION: unscoped pooled search (k=10) on the question text returned no survivor at all and ~24 learning-game projects outside the filter (ProsocialLearn 644204 IA, e-Confidence 732420, weDRAW 732391, 3D Tune-In 644051, INLIFE 732184). A targeted SQL sweep for text-satisfying non-SME projects - serious game / game-based learning in the objective, fundingScheme NOT LIKE 'SME%', plus professional/clinician/surgeon/nurse/staff/worker - returned 5, of which two satisfy the textual ask outright: 653590 AUGGMED (RIA) 'a serious game platform to enable single- and team-based training of end-users with different level of expertise from different organisations responding to terrorist and organised crime threats', and 732358 GATES (IA) 'a serious game-based training platform, in order to train professionals across the agricultural value chain on the use of Smart Farming Technologies'. Dropping the SME Instrument half would therefore give at least three defensible answers - the filter is load-bearing. TEXT side is load-bearing: no stored column records who a product is aimed at or what it lets its users rehearse; that lives only in objective and report free text. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question avoids the gold text's distinctive vocabulary ('serious gaming', 'medical simulation', 'Virtual Reality', 'virtual patients', 'clinical settings', 'flight simulator', 'train'), using 'learning game', 'qualified professionals' and 'rehearse' instead; the scoped rank matrix is consistent - the gold is LAST of the three survivors in lexical (rank 3, behind LINGOKIDS 1 and TheCityGame 2), i.e. the question's wording gives it no lexical advantage. SCOPED RETRIEVABILITY: with scope = the 3 survivors, 781138 ranks 3 in lexical, hybrid and hybrid_rerank, and is absent from dense - present in three of four conditions. pooling_evidence counts come from that scoped search; adjudication itself was the exhaustive 3-survivor read.

record.text: Among the SME-Instrument-funded projects whose product is a learning game, one is aimed at qualified professionals rather than at children or everyday consumers; what does its product let them rehearse?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%serious game%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%game-based learning%') AND (p.objective ILIKE '%learn%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%educat%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%training%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: The one aimed at professionals rather than at children or consumers is abcdeSIM-VR, the SME-1 feasibility project of VirtualMedSchool (VMS) in Rotterdam, built with the Erasmus Medical Centre University Hospital and the SBOH. Its product pairs a Virtual Reality headset with a web-based simulation platform containing a serious game, so that medical and health professionals and trainees can rehearse treating virtual patients in real time under different clinical settings - emergency care skills above all - and can experiment with therapies and watch the physiological response, without any risk to real patients.
record.notes: FILTER: fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' (SME-1/SME-2, the SME Instrument phases; schema_docs lists SME-1 and SME-2 among the 56 fundingScheme values) intersected with a learning-game topic condition over the objective (serious game OR game-based learning, plus a learn/educat/training co-term - the bare gamification term is noisy). Re-executed this pass: 3 survivors, no drift from candidate hybrid-26 (3 under the SME filter, 33 corpus-wide without it). All three are SME-1, EUR 50,000 phase-1 feasibility grants. RUNTIME NOTE: the scoped path filters only structural columns, so at runtime the SME-Instrument half is the filter and the learning-game half falls to retrieval; the question is worded so that this split still works. ADJUDICATION was EXHAUSTIVE (3 <= 20, full get_project_text payload for all three). 781138 abcdeSIM-VR IN: 'a disruptive web-based platform to effectively train medical/health professionals by using serious gaming and medical simulation'; the abcdeSIM-VR adds a Virtual Reality headset so 'the medical trainee ... is fully immersed in a simulated real environment, being able to perform on virtual patients, in real-time, under different clinical settings'; report adds emergency-care skills, self-directed learning for experienced clinicians, and 'trainees are allow to experiment different therapies and see the inmediate response'. 684657 TheCityGame pilot OUT: a consumer mobile 'serious game' that rewards ordinary citizens for recycling, donating clothes, using public transport and keeping utility bills low - end users are the general public, not qualified professionals. 718990 LINGOKIDS OUT: game-based-learning language app whose learners are children aged 2 to 6; parents and educators only get tracking tools and progress reports, so the product does not let a professional rehearse anything. FILTER-DISCRIMINATION: unscoped pooled search (k=10) on the question text returned no survivor at all and ~24 learning-game projects outside the filter (ProsocialLearn 644204 IA, e-Confidence 732420, weDRAW 732391, 3D Tune-In 644051, INLIFE 732184). A targeted SQL sweep for text-satisfying non-SME projects - serious game / game-based learning in the objective, fundingScheme NOT LIKE 'SME%', plus professional/clinician/surgeon/nurse/staff/worker - returned 5, of which two satisfy the textual ask outright: 653590 AUGGMED (RIA) 'a serious game platform to enable single- and team-based training of end-users with different level of expertise from different organisations responding to terrorist and organised crime threats', and 732358 GATES (IA) 'a serious game-based training platform, in order to train professionals across the agricultural value chain on the use of Smart Farming Technologies'. Dropping the SME Instrument half would therefore give at least three defensible answers - the filter is load-bearing. TEXT side is load-bearing: no stored column records who a product is aimed at or what it lets its users rehearse; that lives only in objective and report free text. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question avoids the gold text's distinctive vocabulary ('serious gaming', 'medical simulation', 'Virtual Reality', 'virtual patients', 'clinical settings', 'flight simulator', 'train'), using 'learning game', 'qualified professionals' and 'rehearse' instead; the scoped rank matrix is consistent - the gold is LAST of the three survivors in lexical (rank 3, behind LINGOKIDS 1 and TheCityGame 2), i.e. the question's wording gives it no lexical advantage. record.text: Among the SME-Instrument-funded projects whose product is a learning game, one is aimed at qualified professionals rather than at children or everyday consumers; what does its product let them rehearse?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%serious game%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%game-based learning%') AND (p.objective ILIKE '%learn%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%educat%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%training%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: The one aimed at professionals rather than at children or consumers is abcdeSIM-VR, the SME-1 feasibility project of VirtualMedSchool (VMS) in Rotterdam, built with the Erasmus Medical Centre University Hospital and the SBOH. Its product pairs a Virtual Reality headset with a web-based simulation platform containing a serious game, so that medical and health professionals and trainees can rehearse treating virtual patients in real time under different clinical settings - emergency care skills above all - and can experiment with therapies and watch the physiological response, without any risk to real patients.
record.notes: FILTER: fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%' (SME-1/SME-2, the SME Instrument phases; schema_docs lists SME-1 and SME-2 among the 56 fundingScheme values) intersected with a learning-game topic condition over the objective (serious game OR game-based learning, plus a learn/educat/training co-term - the bare gamification term is noisy). Re-executed this pass: 3 survivors, no drift from candidate hybrid-26 (3 under the SME filter, 33 corpus-wide without it). All three are SME-1, EUR 50,000 phase-1 feasibility grants. RUNTIME NOTE: the scoped path filters only structural columns, so at runtime the SME-Instrument half is the filter and the learning-game half falls to retrieval; the question is worded so that this split still works. ADJUDICATION was EXHAUSTIVE (3 <= 20, full get_project_text payload for all three). 781138 abcdeSIM-VR IN: 'a disruptive web-based platform to effectively train medical/health professionals by using serious gaming and medical simulation'; the abcdeSIM-VR adds a Virtual Reality headset so 'the medical trainee ... is fully immersed in a simulated real environment, being able to perform on virtual patients, in real-time, under different clinical settings'; report adds emergency-care skills, self-directed learning for experienced clinicians, and 'trainees are allow to experiment different therapies and see the inmediate response'. 684657 TheCityGame pilot OUT: a consumer mobile 'serious game' that rewards ordinary citizens for recycling, donating clothes, using public transport and keeping utility bills low - end users are the general public, not qualified professionals. 718990 LINGOKIDS OUT: game-based-learning language app whose learners are children aged 2 to 6; parents and educators only get tracking tools and progress reports, so the product does not let a professional rehearse anything. FILTER-DISCRIMINATION: unscoped pooled search (k=10) on the question text returned no survivor at all and ~24 learning-game projects outside the filter (ProsocialLearn 644204 IA, e-Confidence 732420, weDRAW 732391, 3D Tune-In 644051, INLIFE 732184). A targeted SQL sweep for text-satisfying non-SME projects - serious game / game-based learning in the objective, fundingScheme NOT LIKE 'SME%', plus professional/clinician/surgeon/nurse/staff/worker - returned 5, of which two satisfy the textual ask outright: 653590 AUGGMED (RIA) 'a serious game platform to enable single- and team-based training of end-users with different level of expertise from different organisations responding to terrorist and organised crime threats', and 732358 GATES (IA) 'a serious game-based training platform, in order to train professionals across the agricultural value chain on the use of Smart Farming Technologies'. Dropping the SME Instrument half would therefore give at least three defensible answers - the filter is load-bearing. TEXT side is load-bearing: no stored column records who a product is aimed at or what it lets its users rehearse; that lives only in objective and report free text. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question avoids the gold text's distinctive vocabulary ('serious gaming', 'medical simulation', 'Virtual Reality', 'virtual patients', 'clinical settings', 'flight simulator', 'train'), using 'learning game', 'qualified professionals' and 'rehearse' instead; the scoped rank matrix is consistent - the gold is LAST of the three survivors in lexical (rank 3, behind LINGOKIDS 1 and TheCityGame 2), i.e. the question's wording gives it no lexical advantage. record.text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships on working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose title or objective names working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
record.notes: Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF) AND the topic clause working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (13 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - MEG of working-memory control in young vs old bilinguals, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - working-memory capacity enhancement in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - shared WM/decision-making circuit tested and then extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-8 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 3, NeWMaBIL 4).

record.text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships on working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose title or objective names working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
record.notes: Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF) AND the topic clause working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (13 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - MEG of working-memory control in young vs old bilinguals, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - working-memory capacity enhancement in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - shared WM/decision-making circuit tested and then extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-8 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 3, NeWMaBIL 4).

findings.evidence: A SQL sweep for MSCA-IF% projects that do NOT name working memory in objective or title but whose report text does, combined with an ageing-term match, returned 9 rows; 655423 is the strongest. The 3-survivor set is therefore the whole Dutch-coordinated SME game-learning class, not an artefact of chosen phrases. findings.claim: A second SME-Instrument project satisfies the question as asked. SEEABLE (672124, SME-1) is a learning game for working professionals that lets them rehearse workplace safety, so the question's 'one is aimed at qualified professionals' premise has at least two answers.
findings.evidence: A widened topic condition over SME projects (educational game, learning game, training game, game-based training, edutainment, serious game, game-based learning in objective) returns 8 rows, not the drafter's 3: 684657, 717644 ERXOS, 718357 Smart Library, 718990, 756826 Smart Library SME-2, 781138, 817456 Social Digital Lab, 855417 BLAPP. SEEABLE arrived separately, in the critic's own-wording pooled search (rerank 8) and in a professional-audience sweep. Its objective, read in full: "we have identified the possibility to repurpose this data so that we can provide interactive and context-relevant S&H training via 3D applications... We will develop an application to deliver S&H training to railway workers. It will employ pedagogic strategies in a games environment to demonstrate enhanced learning. We will test it in a classroom environment with real learners". fundingScheme SME-1. Every clause holds: SME-Instrument funded; the product is a learning game; its users are railway and construction workers, not children and not everyday consumers; and what it lets them rehearse is site safety and health procedure in context-relevant 3D. It is invisible to the recorded filter_sql only because that SQL requires the exact strings 'serious game' or 'game-based learning', and the scoped runtime applies only fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%', so SEEABLE is inside the live candidate pool a system searches.
findings.fix_direction: Narrow the audience clause to a licensed clinical audience, or move the discriminating clause onto something SEEABLE cannot claim (virtual patients / physiological response). Either edit needs the survivor re-adjudication redone against the wider term set.
findings.ruling_why: The critic read 672124 SEEABLE's full objective and it satisfies every clause the question asks (SME-1, a learning game, adult workers rather than children or consumers, rehearsing site safety), so the question's 'one is' uniqueness premise has at least two answers and a system that returned SEEABLE would be scored wrong; the drafter's evidence does not refute this because its filter_sql required the literal strings and never saw the project.

findings.claim: Body Interact (710753, SME-1) is a defensible competing answer under a slightly looser reading of 'learning game': described in the same words the gold uses about itself, aimed at the same audience, rehearsing the same thing.
findings.evidence: 710753 objective: "Body InteractTM is an immersive medical 'flight' simulator that allows healthcare professionals (HCPs) to experience responsive real clinical cases in virtual environments... a simulation tool with a scientific algorithm that creates a virtual responsive patient, based on the real physicochemical reactions of the human body, enabling users to download specific clinical cases to solve". The gold's own title is "The flight simulator for Medical and Health Professionals" and the drafter's reference sells the gold on exactly "rehearse treating virtual patients... experiment with therapies and watch the physiological response". Body Interact loses only on the literal token: a scan of objective + all report sections for 'game' returns false in every section for 710753 (true in the objective for 781138 and 672124). Weaker second instance: ADVERSARY 836106 (SME-1), cybersecurity training through a gamified experience for IT managers and developers.
findings.fix_direction: Make the game clause load-bearing in the question text itself so a pure simulator is excluded on the face of the question.
findings.ruling_why: Body Interact 710753 loses only on the literal token 'game' while matching the audience and the exact activity the reference sells the gold on, which is the brief's strained-but-losing alternate reading, and it is load-bearing here because the obvious narrowing of F1 toward a clinical audience or toward virtual patients pulls it straight into contention.

findings.claim: The exhaustiveness claim in notes establishes uniqueness only within a 3-project set that two hand-picked phrases produced, while the class the question names is much larger and the runtime scope is larger still.
findings.evidence: SME projects number 5,734, of which 262 mention game or gamif in the objective. One step of vocabulary widening takes the survivor set from 3 to 8; adding gamified/serious-gaming/simulation-training terms returns 31 SME rows, among them Body Interact 710753, ePT 773124 (Electronic Procedure Trainer for aviation pilots and cabin crew), ADVERSARY 836106 and KG Pro 2.0 827134, all professional-audience training products never adjudicated. findings.fix_direction: Re-run the survivor enumeration with a term set covering the question's own words, adjudicate the resulting set, then re-derive the survivor window and pooling evidence from it.
findings.ruling_why: The gold's own objective phrase is 'serious gaming', which the recorded filter_sql does not match, so the 3-survivor set held together by an accident of a second sentence; scope_size 3 and the EXHAUSTIVE adjudication claim therefore measure uniqueness inside a set two hand-picked phrases produced, not inside the class the question names.

findings.claim: The reference calls the project 'the SME-1 feasibility project of VirtualMedSchool (VMS) in Rotterdam'; the only organization row for 781138 is ABCDE-SIM BV.
findings.evidence: organization rows for 781138: ABCDE-SIM BV | ROTTERDAM | NL | coordinator (sole participant). The VMS/Erasmus MC/SBOH claim traces to the objective text, so it is supported, but the funded legal entity in the database is ABCDE-SIM BV.

record.text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is to study working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
record.notes: Scope wording: 'whose stated aim is to study working memory' matches the filter's topic clause (objective or title), and deliberately excludes fellowships that merely ran a working-memory task while reporting - 655423 NIBSAD (stated aim: 'visuospatial attention and cognitive control processes'; tDCS working-memory task on eighteen healthy elderly in its report) and 844246 AGEING PLASTICITY (stated aim: prefrontal plasticity and resilience against cognitive ageing; retro-cue working memory task in its report) are out of scope by the question's own words. Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF; no MSCA-PF scheme exists in this corpus) AND working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (14 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - title states working memory control in aged bilinguals, MEG in young vs old adults, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - objective states the aim as enhancement of working memory capacity in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - title states decision-making and working memory in health and old age, extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-5 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 2, NeWMaBIL 5).

record.text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is to study working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
record.notes: Scope wording: 'whose stated aim is to study working memory' matches the filter's topic clause (objective or title), and deliberately excludes fellowships that merely ran a working-memory task while reporting - 655423 NIBSAD (stated aim: 'visuospatial attention and cognitive control processes'; tDCS working-memory task on eighteen healthy elderly in its report) and 844246 AGEING PLASTICITY (stated aim: prefrontal plasticity and resilience against cognitive ageing; retro-cue working memory task in its report) are out of scope by the question's own words. Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF; no MSCA-PF scheme exists in this corpus) AND working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (14 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - title states working memory control in aged bilinguals, MEG in young vs old adults, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - objective states the aim as enhancement of working memory capacity in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - title states decision-making and working memory in health and old age, extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-5 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 2, NeWMaBIL 5).

record.reference_answer: SEEDS (Science Engagement to Empower Disadvantaged adoleScents, grant 101006251, started 2021-01-01). It recruited 25 high schools in deprived neighbourhoods across four pilot countries (6 UK, 4 NL, 7 GR, 8 SP), selected 15-18 adolescent ambassadors per country, and had those adolescents co-create the interventions themselves at eight makeathons - activities targeting healthy snacks, more physical activity and less sedentary behaviour, run from January to July 2022 as a way of building their engagement with science.

Runtime note: only the date half is a filterable column on the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) - the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudications: 101006251 SEEDS IN - objective and report describe recruiting high schools in deprived neighbourhoods, 15-18 adolescent ambassadors per country, makeathons where the adolescents co-created interventions on healthy snacks/physical activity/sedentary behaviour, with vegetable consumption the one significant outcome. 101000063 Scientix 4 OUT - a teacher-facing portal, MOOCs and ambassador community for STEM teaching; no pupil-designed activities, no food or exercise. 961665 Robo Wunderkind OUT - an Austrian company commercialising an AI-enabled robotics/coding kit for children. 956124 SellSTEM OUT - MSCA network training researchers on spatial ability deficits and the gender gap in STEM enrolment; children are study participants, not activity designers, and no lifestyle content. 101036166 ReCoN-nect OUT - Romanian European Researchers' Night on the Green Deal, ~60 public events. Adjudications: 101006251 SEEDS IN - objective and report describe recruiting high schools in deprived neighbourhoods, 15-18 adolescent ambassadors per country, makeathons where the adolescents co-created interventions on healthy snacks/physical activity/sedentary behaviour, with vegetable consumption the one significant outcome. 101000063 Scientix 4 OUT - a teacher-facing portal, MOOCs and ambassador community for STEM teaching; no pupil-designed activities, no food or exercise. 961665 Robo Wunderkind OUT - an Austrian company commercialising an AI-enabled robotics/coding kit for children. 956124 SellSTEM OUT - MSCA network training researchers on spatial ability deficits and the gender gap in STEM enrolment; children are study participants, not activity designers, and no lifestyle content. 101036166 ReCoN-nect OUT - Romanian European Researchers' Night on the Green Deal, ~60 public events. Scoped over the 5 survivors SEEDS is rank 1 in all four conditions.

record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to master both the hue and the beam spread of light leaving low-energy lamps by engineering the nanometre-sized emitting particles and the layers around them, rather than relying on conventional lenses?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

record.reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it combines rare-earth nanophosphors with engineered photonic architectures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, corrugated films and optical cavities - so that the chromaticity and the directionality of a light-emitting device's output are set by optical design rather than by altering the emitter's chemistry or by external reflectors and lenses. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.
record.notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'nanophotonics' (one-reading check: 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics' is the only path matching '%nanophotonics%', 62 projects) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-STG' -> 10 survivors, re-executed this pass. Runtime note: the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) can only filter the structural half ('ERC Starting Grant' -> fundingScheme='ERC-STG'); the nanophotonics topic is carried by retrieval, which is how the question is worded. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 10 read at objective+teaser, gold at full payload): 715832 NANOPHOM IN - aims at 'ultimate spectral and angular control over the light emission properties' of LEDs via nanophosphors plus multilayers/surface textures/nano-scatterers, explicitly surpassing 'the limits imposed by conventional optics'. OUT: 637116 ENLIGHTMENT (photonic electrodes to enhance light ABSORPTION in thin solar cells, photodetectors, sensors); 639109 FLATLIGHT (visible-wavelength metasurfaces as ultrathin reconfigurable optical components and modulators); 677470 SEAQUEL (cold structured atomic ensembles for quantum engineering of light); 679841 ORDERin1D (chirality-sorted carbon nanotubes, molecular filling and order); 714151 PSINFONI (particle-surface near-field interactions, optical and Casimir forces); 802682 MODES (nonlinear multimode processes in fibres, chips and nanoparticles); 802986 aQUARiUM (epsilon-near-zero rolled-up metamaterials for quantum light-matter interaction); 853500 NanoGraphy (plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic nanolithography); 948804 CHANSON (chiral semiconductor nanophotonics for molecular sensing). DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the question text): 657434 PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST) satisfies the textual ask outright - 'full spectral and angular control over the emission properties' using 'colloidal quantum dots or nanophosphors' plus 'surface textures and colloidal scatterers' for 'precise control on the intensity, angular distribution and color quality of light emission' - and fails the filter; 798697 NEXTLEDs (MSCA-IF) is a second, weaker counter-example (colloidal quantum wells for LEDs with 'exceptionally high colour purity' and enhanced light outcoupling). So dropping the scheme filter changes the answer. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records what a project does with light emission; the filter alone leaves 10 candidates. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question uses 'hue', 'beam spread', 'low-energy lamps', 'nanometre-sized emitting particles' and avoids the gold's distinctive vocabulary (nanophosphor, LED, photonic, solid-state lighting, chromaticity, angular/directional, spectral). Unscoped, the lexical condition did NOT return 715832 in its top-10 (its lexical rank 1 was 899861 BEAMOLED); dense, hybrid and hybrid_rerank all ranked it 1. Scoped lexical rank is 1, but the scope holds only 10 projects so all survivors rank in every condition - that in-scope rank is not evidence against the paraphrase label.

record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to master both the hue and the beam spread of light leaving low-energy lamps by engineering the nanometre-sized emitting particles and the layers around them, rather than relying on conventional lenses?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

record.reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it combines rare-earth nanophosphors with engineered photonic architectures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, corrugated films and optical cavities - so that the chromaticity and the directionality of a light-emitting device's output are set by optical design rather than by altering the emitter's chemistry or by external reflectors and lenses. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.

record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to do away with the lenses and reflectors added onto low-energy lamps by placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings - stacked layers, patterned surfaces and resonant cavities - so that the tint and the beam spread of the light are fixed by those surroundings rather than by changing what the particles themselves are made of?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

record.reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it puts rare-earth nanophosphors inside engineered optical structures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, nanoimprinted corrugations and optical cavities - and shows that those surroundings alone set the chromaticity and the directionality of the device's output, 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', replacing the reflectors and lenses normally added as secondary optical elements. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.
record.notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'nanophotonics' (one-reading check: 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics' is the only path matching '%nanophotonics%', 62 projects) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-STG' -> 10 survivors, re-executed this pass. Runtime note: the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) can only filter the structural half ('ERC Starting Grant' -> fundingScheme='ERC-STG'); the nanophotonics topic is carried by retrieval, which is how the question is worded. LOW note on scope width: the enumerated survivor set is narrower than the runtime's executable scope (all ERC-STG projects), so ERC-STG projects tagged under other euroSciVoc leaves - e.g. 849229 CQWLED (nanocrystals / colors / optoelectronics) - are reachable at runtime but not enumerated here; CQWLED is excluded by the question's own words (see ADJUDICATION), so this is a recorded width note, not a gold gap. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 10 survivors read at objective+teaser, gold at full payload; re-adjudicated against the current wording): 715832 NANOPHOM IN - 'exploits new ways of controlling the emission characteristics of nanophosphors, surpassing the limits imposed by conventional optics', design 'based on multilayers, surface textures and nano-scatterers', and the report states the control comes 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', with reflectors and lenses named as the secondary optical elements being replaced. OUT: 637116 ENLIGHTMENT (photonic electrodes to enhance light ABSORPTION in thin solar cells, photodetectors, sensors); 639109 FLATLIGHT (visible-wavelength metasurfaces as ultrathin reconfigurable optical components and modulators, not emission from a lamp's emitting particles); 677470 SEAQUEL (cold structured atomic ensembles for quantum engineering of light); 679841 ORDERin1D (chirality-sorted carbon nanotubes, molecular filling and order); 714151 PSINFONI (particle-surface near-field interactions, optical and Casimir forces); 802682 MODES (nonlinear multimode processes in fibres, chips and nanoparticles); 802986 aQUARiUM (epsilon-near-zero rolled-up metamaterials for quantum light-matter interaction); 853500 NanoGraphy (plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic nanolithography); 948804 CHANSON (chiral semiconductor nanophotonics for molecular sensing). NEAR-MISSES EXCLUDED BY THE QUESTION'S OWN WORDS: 798697 NEXTLEDs is titled 'Chemical Engineering of Atomically-Flat Colloidal Quantum Wells' and works by synthesizing the emitters themselves - the mechanism the question explicitly rules out - and is MSCA-IF, failing the scheme filter too; 849229 CQWLED likewise guides 'chemistry and shape' of its nanocrystals, never opposes itself to lenses or reflectors (its foils are total internal reflection and EQE), and its 'layers' are the emitter superlattices rather than engineered surroundings. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text): 657434 PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST) satisfies the textual ask outright and ranks dense 1 / hybrid 1 - 'integrating novel optical nanostructures and emitters, such as colloidal quantum dots or nanophosphors ... preparation and processing strategies, based on surface textures and colloidal scatterers, to attain large area optical nanostructures ... precise control on the intensity, angular distribution and color quality of light emission' - and it fails the ERC-STG filter, so dropping the filter changes the answer. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records what a project does with light emission; the filter alone leaves 10 candidates. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question uses 'tint', 'beam spread', 'low-energy lamps', 'stacked layers', 'patterned surfaces', 'resonant cavities' and avoids the gold's distinctive vocabulary (nanophosphor, LED, photonic, solid-state lighting, chromaticity, directionality, spectral, angular, integrated photonic systems). Unscoped on the current wording the lexical condition did NOT return 715832 in its top-10 (lexical rank 1 was 896410 OPAN) while dense ranked it 2, hybrid 3 and hybrid_rerank 2. Scoped lexical rank 1 is uninformative because the scope holds only 10 projects, so every survivor ranks in every condition.

evidence:
ROUND 2 (post-fix). evidence_carried_forward, disclosed by the drafter: (1) the ten survivors' texts were read in the first pass and not re-fetched - the survivor set is byte-identical because filter_sql was untouched, and the re-adjudication was redone against the new wording; (2) the counter-example texts and scheme values for 657434 PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST) and 798697 NEXTLEDs (MSCA-IF) were not re-fetched, though PhoLED re-appeared in this pass's unscoped search; (3) the euroSciVoc one-reading query and the filter enumeration were not re-run by hand, precheck_record having re-executed filter_sql to the identical 10 ids; (4) FLAGGED BY THE DRAFTER ITSELF: it never fetched 849229 CQWLED's text at all, so its exclusion of CQWLED rests on the critic's relayed quotes plus CQWLED's absence from this pass's unscoped top-k.

Gold 715832 NANOPHOM - the passages that satisfy each clause of the new wording, verbatim:
- 'do away with the lenses and reflectors added onto low-energy lamps': report summary - "the limited control over color quality and directionality of LED light emission that standard materials and reflectors and lenses, typically employed as secondary optical elements, provide. NANOPHOM seeks to surpass the limits imposed by geometrical optics in the radiation shaping of light-emitting devices"; objective - "surpassing the limits imposed by conventional optics".
- 'placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings - stacked layers, patterned surfaces and resonant cavities': objective - "The new optical design of these devices will be based on multilayers, surface textures and nano-scatterers of controlled composition, size and shape"; report workPerformed - "the interaction between resonant optical modes and the natural emission of nanophosphors integrated in an optical cavity"; "the periodic corrugation of nanophosphors films by nanoimprinting techniques allows a more efficient extraction of light in specific directions".
- 'rather than by changing what the particles themselves are made of': report workPerformed - "such properties can be tuned using integrated photonic systems, as opposed to conventional methods based on chemical engineering of the emitters" and "precise control over the chromaticity and directionality of their emitted light without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters"; finalResults - "NANOPHOM integrates a series of photonic approaches that control light-matter interaction at the sub-wavelength scale to tailor the emission of nanomaterials without altering their chemical composition".
- 'tint and beam spread': objective - "ultimate spectral and angular control over the light emission properties"; "i) directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone; ii) omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light".

The two named near-misses, judged against the question's own words:
- 798697 NEXTLEDs - EXCLUDED twice over. Title "Chemical Engineering of Atomically-Flat Colloidal Quantum Wells for Next-Generation Light-Emitting Devices"; method "systematically synthesize advanced heterostructures of colloidal NPLs by precisely engineering their surfaces" - changing what the emitting particles are made of, which the question now explicitly rules out - and it is MSCA-IF, so it also fails the scheme filter. Under the new wording it fell out of three of four unscoped conditions (dense 6 only; previously dense 5 / hybrid 5).
- 849229 CQWLED - EXCLUDED by the question's own words on both clauses: its nanocrystals have "chemistry and shape guided by our calculations", the mechanism the question rules out, and nothing in the quoted text sets its work against lenses or reflectors added onto a lamp (its foils are total internal reflection and external quantum efficiency). Under the new wording it does not appear in the unscoped pooled top-k of any of the four conditions. Caveat as disclosed: the drafter did not fetch its text this round.

why_good: The question discriminates on the filter: on the current wording the top unscoped dense and hybrid hit is PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST), which satisfies the textual ask outright, so a system that ignores 'ERC Starting Grant' returns the wrong single project. Inside the ten nanophotonics ERC Starting Grants exactly one, NANOPHOM, matches the specific mechanism asked for - emitting particles left chemically untouched while engineered surroundings replace the lamp's added lenses and reflectors - and that mechanism is stated only in free text, so neither channel alone settles it. It fills the hybrid axes fundingScheme=ERC-STG and euroSciVoc engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics (10 survivors out of 62 nanophotonics projects). The L1 filter-read label is arithmetic: |gold| = 1, read from one survivor's text, 10 survivors inside the 2-10 window.

findings.claim: 849229 CQWLED is an ERC Starting Grant that set out to control both the colour and the emission direction of light from LEDs using nanometre-sized emitting particles, and it is not in the enumerated survivor set - so a system running the real scoped path can reach it and be scored wrong.
findings.evidence: A SQL sweep over ERC-STG projects for emission x colour x directionality language returns exactly two rows, 715832 and 849229. CQWLED report: "the CQD-based LEDs possess extremely high color purity ... it is not yet possible to control the emission directionality perpendicular to the substrate plane in the CQD superlattices". Its absence from the survivors is a tagging artefact - its euroSciVoc paths are nanocrystals, colors and optoelectronics rather than the nanophotonics leaf. Retrievable in scope: dense 3 / rerank 3 on the critic's round-1 reformulation.
findings.fix_direction: Tighten the question so the two clauses CQWLED fails become part of the ask rather than trailing qualifiers.
findings.ruling_why: Round 1: CQWLED is an ERC-STG project the survivor set never enumerated, reachable and retrievable at the real runtime scope, so a live competitor; MID rather than HIGH because it never opposes itself to lenses and its 'layers' are the emitter nanocrystals themselves. CLEARED IN ROUND 2 on the critic's own executed evidence rather than defended: it read CQWLED in full against the new wording and found its colour and direction come from the particles' own chemistry and shape ("synthesized semiconductor nanocrystals with chemistry and shape guided by our calculations", layer-controlled colloidal quantum wells), with no surrounding photonic structure and no lens or reflector anywhere in its objective or report - exactly what the new clause rules out - and it fell to dense 20 on the fresh reformulation.

findings.claim: The question attributed the result to 'engineering the nanometre-sized emitting particles and the layers around them', but NANOPHOM's stated claim is that it achieves this WITHOUT engineering the emitters, so a system that reads the gold text carefully had textual grounds to reject the gold.
findings.evidence: Report workPerformed: "such properties can be tuned using integrated photonic systems, as opposed to conventional methods based on chemical engineering of the emitters" and "precise control over the chromaticity and directionality of their emitted light without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters". The draft's own reference repeated the disclaimer, so the entry contradicted itself between question text and reference. Better-fitting competitors under the old clause: 798697 NEXTLEDs, titled "Chemical Engineering of Atomically-Flat Colloidal Quantum Wells", and 849229 CQWLED.
findings.fix_direction: Reword the mechanism clause to the gold's actual approach without importing its vocabulary.
findings.ruling_why: Round 1: the question contradicted itself between text and reference and the discriminating clause pointed partly away from its own gold; MID rather than HIGH because the lenient reading survived on the nanoimprinted corrugation and because NEXTLEDs is MSCA-IF and genuinely excluded by the scheme filter. CLEARED IN ROUND 2: the rewritten clause states the gold's actual approach and the reference now matches, with the disclaiming string "without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters" verbatim in 715832's workPerformed.

findings.claim: The enumerated survivor set is the nanophotonics tag intersected with ERC-STG (10 ids), but a scoped run searches all 2,771 ERC-STG projects, so the exhaustive adjudication covers less than the question's own scope.
findings.evidence: COUNT(*) FROM project WHERE fundingScheme='ERC-STG' = 2771 versus survivor_count 10. In round 2 the critic closed the gap for the current wording with an exhaustive non-embedding sweep of all 2,771 ERC-STG projects requiring a structure term AND a particle-emitter term AND a direction term AND a colour term: four rows - 715832 NANOPHOM, 639088 SeSaMe (structural colour in cellulose/chitin biomimetic materials), 714968 VISIRday (passive daytime radiative cooling), 638001 Dynamic Nano (nanoplasmonic building blocks for sensing and catalysis) - none of the three non-gold hits a light-emitting device. This is a gap to re-check whenever the text changes, not one the survivor enumeration closes.

The drafter flagged this and the critic confirms it, but it has not become a lexical give-away: on the critic's heaviest paraphrase the gold's lexical rank was 6, behind BEAMOLED 899861 at 1.

findings.claim: FLATLIGHT 639109 is the survivor the fronted anti-lens clause now fits best, which explains its scoped hybrid_rerank rank 1.
findings.evidence: Read in full this pass rather than carried forward: "unlike refractive optical components, the wavefront is modified without propagation"; "achromatic optical devices ... ruling out some of the limitations of conventional refractive and diffractive optics". Still a defensible OUT: it has no light-emitting nanoparticles at all (its actives are InGaAlN films and VCSELs) and its demonstrated devices are metalenses and LiDAR, not lamps, so it fails the 'placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings' and 'low-energy lamps' clauses on its own text.

A wording repair touching neither gold, filter, survivor set nor level. The entry now measures what its cell claims: the scheme filter is load-bearing (PhoLED 657434 and PEROGAN sit at or above the gold on both fresh unscoped reformulations and are excluded only by fundingScheme, re-confirmed by executed lookup), the text half is load-bearing, and the gold is uniquely correct over the scope a scoped run actually searches rather than over the 10 enumerated survivors - the critic's exhaustive sweep of all 2,771 ERC-STG projects returned four rows and read the three non-gold ones out as structural colour, nanoplasmonic sensing and radiative cooling, none a light-emitting device. Both round-1 MIDs were closed by the wording change, and the one claim the drafter flagged as unmeasured (CQWLED's own text) was settled by the critic reading it, so no untested assertion carries into the bank.
